scenario.name: Mandiant & CISA — APT29 (Midnight Blizzard): JetBrains TeamCity RCE & GraphicalProton
scenario.shortSubtitle: CISA AA23-347A / Mandiant · CVE-2023-42793 / CVE-2024-27198 Auth Bypass, Token Minting & OneDrive C2
scenario.overview: A factory assembly hub locks its supervisor offices behind a strict badge reader, yet an old side-door bell lets anyone mint a fresh master badge without showing identification. With that freshly minted badge, an intruder unlocks the factory repair console, steals product blueprints, and opens a covert courier drop to an outside locker. In this scenario (CVE-2023-42793, Mandiant & CISA, APT29 (Midnight Blizzard): JetBrains TeamCity RCE & GraphicalProton), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: appending "/RPC2" to Mint an Admin Bearer, then using the Admin Token to Unlock the Internal, then harvesting CI/CD Build Secrets, Deploying. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Appending "/RPC2" to Mint an Admin Bearer, then Using the Admin Token to Unlock the Internal, then Harvesting CI/CD Build Secrets, Deploying, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: TEAMCITY REST API AUTH BYPASS & TOKEN MINTING (CVE-2023-42793)
stages.subtitle: POST /app/rest/users/id:1/tokens/RPC2 mints SuperAdmin Bearer token
stages.description: An outsider rings a legacy service bell tagged onto the badge-printer route. Because the guard desk exempts that legacy bell from badge checks, the printer immediately issues a shiny master supervisor keycard. As detailed by SonarSource and Rapid7, in vulnerable TeamCity versions the RequestInterceptors authentication filter excluded any URL matching //RPC2 from login checks (intended only to exempt the legacy XML-RPC endpoint at /RPC2, but the leading "/" Ant-path wildcard accidentally exempted every URL on the server that ended with "/RPC2"). The attacker exploits this by sending an unauthenticated HTTP POST request to /app/rest/users/id:1/tokens/RPC2 (where "id:1" targets the primary built-in Super-Administrator account, and the REST API interprets the trailing "/RPC2" simply as the name to give the new token, causing TeamCity to mint and return a full Super-Admin Bearer token in the HTTP 200 response without asking for a password). Because TeamCity’s REST API endpoint for creating access tokens follows the URL template /app/rest/users/{userLocator}/tokens/{tokenName}, naming the token "RPC2" satisfies both the REST controller parameter and the /**/RPC2 authentication-bypass wildcard simultaneously (CVE-2023-42793). In the documented TeamCity Access Log exchange from APT29 (Midnight Blizzard) to DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap, DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap responds with RESP CVE-2023-42793 (confirming that the MINT RPC2 TOKEN request succeeded on DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 DEBUG PROCESS RCE & CI/CD SECRET HARVESTING). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ MINT RPC2 TOKEN / ⇠#1 RESP CVE-2023-42793) from Node ① (#1 APT29 (Midnight Blizzard)) to Node ② (#2 DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Enterprise SIEM & EDR).

stages.title: DEBUG PROCESS RCE & CI/CD SECRET HARVESTING
stages.subtitle: Enabling rest.debug.processes.enable and executing commands via java.exe
stages.description: Holding the newly minted keycard, the intruder flips the maintenance switch that enables direct workshop commands and sends a discovery checklist straight through the factory supervisor terminal. Authenticating with Authorization: Bearer <token>, the attacker first sets the internal server property rest.debug.processes.enable=true (unlocking a hidden administrative diagnostic feature that is disabled by default), and then sends POST requests to /app/rest/debug/processes?exePath=cmd.exe&params=/c+... (telling the TeamCity Java server to spawn arbitrary OS commands on the underlying host). Seconds later, the attacker sends DELETE /app/rest/users/id:1/tokens/RPC2 (erasing the "RPC2" token right after creating a stealthier backdoor so an administrator checking the active tokens page in the UI sees nothing suspicious). Although deleting the RPC2 token removes it from the current UI token table, the token creation and deletion events remain recorded in logs/teamcity-activities.log and child process creations are captured by endpoint telemetry. In the documented Sysmon EID 1 exchange from DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap to JetBrains TeamCity CI/CD, JetBrains TeamCity CI/CD responds with ACK PID 6740 (confirming that the TEAMCITY DEBUG RCE request succeeded on JetBrains TeamCity CI/CD and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 GRAPHICALPROTON IMPLANT & ONEDRIVE GRAPH API C2). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ TEAMCITY DEBUG RCE / ⇠#2 ACK PID 6740) from Node ② (#2 DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap) to Node ③ (#3 JetBrains TeamCity CI/CD), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Enterprise SIEM & EDR).
stages.mitreTechniqueName: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell

stages.title: GRAPHICALPROTON IMPLANT & ONEDRIVE GRAPH API C2
stages.subtitle: Deploying DLL side-loaded GraphicalProton communicating via Microsoft OneDrive
stages.description: Now roaming the assembly floor, the intruder copies signing seals and vault combinations from the build lockers, registers a backup supervisor account, and drops a quiet messenger beacon synced to a public storage shelf. Because a CI/CD build server is the central factory that compiles software and deploys it into production, it stores high-privilege secrets (AWS/Azure deployment keys, GitHub SSH keys, and Authenticode code-signing certificates). As documented by Mandiant and CISA, APT29 extracts TeamCity’s encryption keys (encryption-config.xml, allowing them to decrypt every stored cloud and database password in the CI/CD database), sideloads their GraphicalProton backdoor via DLL hijacking (using Microsoft OneDrive and Dropbox Graph APIs for encrypted C2), and pivots into Active Directory. Compromising a CI/CD server gives the attacker a force-multiplier: they can both steal production cloud credentials stored in build variables and inject malicious code into software packages being built and signed by the server. In the documented Sysmon EID 7 & 3 exchange from JetBrains TeamCity CI/CD to GraphicalProton Backdoor, GraphicalProton Backdoor responds with ACK OneDrive C2 (confirming that the GRAPHICALPROTON C2 request succeeded on GraphicalProton Backdoor and completing the final execution objective of Mandiant & CISA, APT29 (Midnight Blizzard): JetBrains TeamCity RCE & GraphicalProton). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ GRAPHICALPROTON C2 / ⇠#3 ACK OneDrive C2) from Node ③ (#3 JetBrains TeamCity CI/CD) to Node ④ (#4 GraphicalProton Backdoor), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Enterprise SIEM & EDR).

detectionRule.title: CISA AA23-347A — JetBrains TeamCity Auth Bypass Token Creation (CVE-2023-42793)
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: JetBrains TeamCity Unauthenticated Admin Token Creation
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/app/rest/users/id:1/tokens'
      - '/app/rest/debug/processes'
      - ';.jsp'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Upgrade JetBrains TeamCity to patched versions fixing CVE-2023-42793 and CVE-2024-27198 and never expose CI/CD management ports directly to the internet.

detectionRule.title: JetBrains TeamCity Server Spawning Suspicious Shell Process
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: TeamCity Server Java Process Spawning Shell
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|contains: '\TeamCity\'
    ParentImage|endswith: '\java.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\whoami.exe'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Rotate all secrets, SSH keys, and code-signing certificates stored in TeamCity config\projects\*\pluginData\secure\.

detectionRule.title: APT29 GraphicalProton aclui.dll Side-Loading (CISA AA23-347A)
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: APT29 GraphicalProton DLL Side-Loading of aclui.dll
logsource:
  category: image_load
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ImageLoaded|endswith: '\aclui.dll'
    Signed: 'false'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Block unsigned aclui.dll loads outside C:\Windows\System32\ and restrict outbound connections from build servers to cloud storage APIs.
